blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

items: High Courts (Article 226) have a wider writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court (Article 32), as High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights.
Mandamus cannot be issued against a private individual, the President of India, or State Governors.
Quo-Warranto is the only writ that can be filed by any interested citizen, not strictly limited to the aggrieved person.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Writs are written legal orders issued by the Supreme Court under Article 32 and High Courts under Article 226 to protect Fundamental Rights.
The five types of writs are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
Habeas Corpus literally means 'to have the body of' and protects citizens against unlawful detention by both public and private entities.
Mandamus is a command issued to a public authority to perform an official duty they failed or refused to execute.
Certiorari is both preventive and curative, allowing higher courts to quash orders of lower courts or tribunals.
